positions.name: FTAI Aviation Ltd.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit Fri 9/18 at the close, or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Announced a $500 million share repurchase program; the stock printed 181.06 pre-market versus a 176.44 close, +2.62%. Against a $18.1B market cap the authorisation is ~2.8% of shares, and it lands with the stock 44% below its $323.51 February 52-week high.
positions.risks: A buyback authorisation is not a buyback - nothing obliges FTAI to execute. The stock is down 44% from its high for reasons the announcement does not address, and jet fuel running ~70% above 2025 with carriers cutting routes pressures the leasing and aftermarket engine business directly. 44.7x book is expensive for an asset lessor.

positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit Fri 9/18 at the close, or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit

positions.name: TORM plc
positions.exitRule: Catalyst-defined - flat on a formal Hafnia offer or any disclosure that the stake has stopped growing, on the Fri 9/18 close at the latest, or on a 5% stop
positions.catalyst: Hafnia raised its TORM holding to 18.22% on 9/16 after buying another 4.5 million shares - a named strategic acquirer accumulating toward a control position in product tankers, the sector with the single best fundamental backdrop on the board. TRMD prints 35.99 pre-market versus a 34.93 close, +3.03%, on 8.4m shares traded Tuesday against a 1.3m 30-day average. Diesel at a record $6.26/gal and Saudi Aramco cancelling European cargoes is what the freight rates are actually pricing.
positions.risks: Entry is 0.14% above the $35.938 52-week high set 9/9, so there is no overhead supply and no reference level under the trade. An 18.22% stake is not an offer and Hafnia has made no bid; stake-building can stall for quarters. The $3.58B market cap is the smallest in the book and it went ex-dividend $2.40 on 9/10, so the tape is still digesting that. UK-domiciled operator listed in the US.
positions.driver: Tier 1 - stake accumulation by a named strategic buyer

positions.name: Generac Holdings Inc.
positions.exitRule: Catalyst-defined - flat on the first analyst PT revision that prices the deal in, on any fade back below the $200.93 warrant strike, or on the Fri 9/18 close at the latest; 5% stop from entry
positions.catalyst: Amazon and Generac signed a long-term supply agreement for up to $8 billion of backup power generators for Amazon data centers, disclosed in an 8-K filed 9/16. Amazon received a warrant for up to 1,693,745 shares at $200.9266, of which 307,954 vested immediately and the rest vest against cumulative payments up to $8B. Initial deliveries are guided at $2.4B across 2027-28. GNRC printed 230.07 pre-market versus a 175.11 close, +31.4%.
positions.risks: Entering a +31% gap - the single largest execution risk in the book, and gaps this size routinely give back a third of the move intraday. Only $2.4B of the $8B is contracted deliveries; the rest is a vesting schedule, not an order book. The warrant is dilutive at $200.93 and caps upside as it vests. GNRC is still 22% below a $296.44 June 52-week high and this entry breaks the book's 15%-of-prior-close guard, which is documented rather than hidden.

positions.name: Vertiv Holdings Co

VRT prints 248.75 versus a 239.41 close, +3.90% - the strongest pre-market bid in the power complex.
positions.risks: This is the second entry in VRT in three sessions; yesterday's intraday version made $15.40 and the re-entry is 3.9% above where it was closed, so the book is chasing its own exit. 19.0x book and 53.1x earnings with the 10-year at 5.01% and the Fed guiding to one more hike. Intraday only.

positions.name: GE Vernova Inc.

positions.name: Arm Holdings plc
positions.exitRule: Overnight (next-day open) - flat on the Fri 9/18 open

positions.name: Micron Technology, Inc.

Micron is the only US-listed front-end DRAM/HBM manufacturer, so a domestic-memory-supply scramble reprices it first. MU prints 946.25 versus a 926.55 close, +2.13%.
positions.risks: 24.6% below a $1,255 June 52-week high after a 6x run off a $154.65 low - the position has no valuation cushion and a very long way to fall. The catalyst is a competitor's unconfirmed talks, which SK Hynix has already publicly hedged. Intraday only for exactly that reason.

positions.name: Astera Labs, Inc.

positions.name: Snap Inc.
positions.exitRule: Overnight (next-day open) - flat on the Fri 9/18 open
positions.catalyst: Snap announced on 9/16 that it is taking its $2,195 Specs AR glasses into the enterprise market with three named partners: Salesforce brings Agentforce onto the device, Nvidia makes its XR AI framework compatible so the assistant runs on a local company workstation, and AWS supplies the voice-command assistant. Snap also unveiled Specs Intelligence, a consumer tier, with retail demos starting in October. SNAP prints 5.91 versus a 5.72 close, +3.32%.
positions.risks: The only sub-$10 name in the book - not a penny stock at a ~$10B cap, but the lowest-quality balance sheet and the widest relative spread here. A hardware pivot into enterprise is a multi-year story with no revenue attached to this announcement, and Snap has repeatedly failed to commercialise hardware (Spectacles). Held overnight into Friday.
